To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
In mobile multiuser diversity systems the upper bound of achievable data rate is defined by the feedback error rate and delay.

the sum capacity of mobile multiuser diversity systems is mainly defined by the feedback latency, that the feedback error rate is only a second order effect, that the impact of both error and delay is much higher than the impact of the feedback overhead and that the feedback delay is the most critical parameter in the design of future multiuser diversity systems.

the sum capacity of mobile systems with multiuser diversity scheduling and imperfect channel feedback is primarily determined by the feedback delay and that the feedback delay is a more important parameter than the feedback error rate.

studying the impact of feedback errors and delay on the sum capacity of mobile multiuser diversity systems.
the study of the sum capacity of multiuser diversity systems in mobile environments.

feedback delay is more detrimental than feedback error, and that the impact of feedback delay is independent of the feedback error probability.
the sum capacity of multiuser systems is limited by feedback delay, and not by the feedback error rate.

in mobile multiuser diversity systems with feedback delay, the sum capacity is primarily determined by the feedback delay, which makes reducing the feedback delay one of the most crucial design goals in future wireless networks.

in mobile scenarios, feedback delay is the most important performance limiting factor for multiuser diversity systems.
feedback delay is the main bottleneck in the sum capacity of mobile systems.

the sum capacity of mobile multiuser systems is very sensitive to the feedback delay and that reducing the feedback delay to the order of the coherence time is crucial to achieve the full multiuser diversity gains.
